problem: VLMs and sequence-based instruction generators (e.g. NavComposer) struggle with spatial grounding in dense, cluttered, quasi-static environments (grocery stores, warehouses). They reference transient visual objects and under-specify route geometry, and dense visual features go stale.
motivation: Real-world navigation and search in such spaces depends on stable semantic landmarks and topological transitions rather than metric commands. A lightweight representation built from one consumer mobile scan could serve search, localization and instruction generation for humans (including blind and low-vision users) and robots without infrastructure such as beacons or RFID.
key_idea: Distill a consumer RGB-D scan into a 2D occupancy map, extract a skeleton topology graph, and anchor VLM-labelled product semantics to it, giving one shared representation for search, one-shot localization, zone classification and landmark-rich route instructions.
insight: Separating deterministic geometry (topology, A*) from VLM semantic reasoning yields more stable instructions than raw RGB sequences or coordinate-only prompts. Naive coordinate prompting degrades on long routes (2.73), while GIST holds 4.59. The visual ablation shows semantics plus light visual grounding is what matters: Naive+Map has landmark utility of 2.89 and safety of 3.00, while Topo-only or Map-only (4.55/4.49) match or beat the full composite image (4.43), suggesting less visual clutter helps.
method: Mobile data to occupancy: 8,668 subsampled RGB-D frames with ARKit odometry are height-sliced into a 0.05 m/px 2D occupancy grid, avoiding SLAM backends.

Keyframe and object extraction: DINOv3 cosine filter (threshold 0.85) reduces to 660 keyframes; YOLOv9 (SKU-110K) detects products, keeping the sharpest crop and the most diverse crop per frame; YOLOv9-COCO handles produce.

Semantic map: crops are tiled into 5x5 mosaics and labelled by gemini-3-flash-preview (name, brand, packaging, category, blur flag). Positions come from depth unprojection and are snapped to shelf edges with Bresenham ray refinement.

Topology: Zhang-Suen skeletonization gives a graph with junctions and turns (60° threshold), clustered and pruned, with edges verified by line-of-sight. Products are bound via perpendicular projection to virtual nodes.

Zone classification and intent-aware search: the VLM assigns 18 zones; a KD-tree inverse-distance-squared vote (k=5) paints free space. Search returns exact, alternative and related items, with zone-median fallback when the item is unmapped.

One-shot semantic localizer: 0.5 m cells x 8 orientation bins are raycast (20 rays) and product metadata is encoded with DistilBERT. A query image goes through YOLOv9, the VLM and DistilBERT, then cosine matching returns top-k poses.

Visually-grounded routing: an A* path over the graph is chunked into turns (>30°). An annotated map image, route segments and visible landmarks with left/right sides are given to the VLM, which forbids cardinal directions.

setting.backbone: gemini-3-flash-preview (frozen VLM) + YOLOv9 (SKU-110K / COCO) + DINOv3 vitb16 + DistilBERT
setting.training_data: none (training-free; uses pretrained models and a single mobile scan of one 3,500 sq ft grocery store)
setting.observation: consumer iPhone LiDAR RGB-D (960x720 RGB, 256x192 depth) with ARKit 6-DoF odometry; single smartphone image for localization
setting.action_space: none; outputs natural-language route instructions over a topology graph (A* path, turn commands and distances)
setting.privileged: none at test time; the full store is pre-scanned offline to build the map

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmark is used. Own-benchmark results are: localization on 20 frames (top-5 error 1.45 ± 1.29 m over all frames, 1.04 ± 0.80 m on correct-zone frames); LLM-judge instruction score for GIST (Visual) of 4.43/5 over 15 scenarios; in-situ probe with N=5 and 80% success (8/10 tasks). NavComposer per-criterion scores appear only in a figure.
results: GIST (Visual) scores 4.43/5 on the LLM-judged multi-criteria evaluation across 15 store scenarios, above NavComposer and Naive Gemini at every route-length bucket. It scores 4.59 on long routes versus 3.75 and 2.73. The one-shot localizer gets 80% zone accuracy and 1.04 m top-5 error on correct-zone frames. In a formative study (N=5), verbal cues alone gave an 80% success rate (8/10 tasks).
limitations: Chest-level scanning misses bottom and top shelf items (field-of-view clipping), which caused both failed user trials; the zone fallback could not help for isolated items.
The localizer suffers semantic aliasing from mirrored viewpoints (top-1 error 3.78 m), so it is only suited to global initialization; evaluation used just 20 frames.
Evaluation is small and single-site: one store, 15 scenarios judged by an LLM, N=5 graduate students and no blind or low-vision users.
